title: Playing bass: first job, Delpit's, and later bass work in California
summary: His first bass job came from Ernie Cagnolatti. Later he played bass with Johnny Sincere, Adolphe Alexander and an Army friend, and with Joe's Dixieland group in the Southern California Hot Jazz Society.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: You say you play bass and violin.

Oh yes, well bass, oh well incidentally I want to tell you this, my first job on bass violin, Ernie Canguletta gave me that job. I was tickled pink, I guess I would have played for nothing. Because you know I was so tickled. My little buddy, we played at Delpit's I think it was, I don't know if the place is operating yet, that was in Uptown Station, like around, oh I don't know exactly, a couple of the basses above the new bass and canal. Kaliop I think. Oh yeah. Kaliop and Franklin was it?

I think it was Kaliop and Franklin, well that's the first job I ever played on bass. And then I like bass. Now I've played the most, I've worked with Johnny Sincere on bass too. You know a couple of little parties like that? He came down and I was delivering, I mean I was delivering, I was running cab then. I worked with Johnny and Tats, you know Adolph Alexander? Oh yes, yeah. Well I flew around with them and worked on bass then. I didn't do too much on bass because I was really busy mostly on my horn most of the time. Now since I've been here I've worked on bass a lot. I've worked with a guy called Jonas Hodge, I don't know if you know him. He's, well he's from Minden, Louisiana and I happened to be his sergeant when we were in the Army together. And I worked with him on bass. I worked with him maybe about seven or eight months. That was during the time I was delivering mail. Well he was going out of town, as long as he didn't go too far I went with him, you know. Then I stopped and I played other jobs on bass around here. A pretty good bit anyhow, you know. Because bass financially speaking when you're not working regularly I have a better house financially with it. I do better. Oh yes I do better with it. But otherwise I always still want to play my horn so I see. When I joined this little club, you know this little Southern California Hot Jazz Society, a lot of those senior guys playing Dixieland. But to be honest I never, I had never known too much about Dixieland to play it. But I could always sort of keep some of those numbers in my mind. And some of those, no kidding, because Big One had picked it up, I practically knew them. A lot of numbers the guy asked me, you know this number? I said no. And they'd probably pick it up or something, then I turned around and said yes. It's because I didn't know them by name. Now I don't say I knew all of them, Bill. But gosh, I mean it didn't take me no time to play them because I've heard them, it seemed to be instilled in you. Why haven't you heard about them? You heard them at all the dances when you were a kid, when I was a kid. And being so, you know, liking music so much I guess that's why it didn't take me long to run them. I think I played practically the majority of the Dixieland, but I know, and then Joe, Joe Dazberg, he has a book with them too. When did you join Joe? I did, I joined Joe and I just joined Joe about, I'd say 15 months ago, about 15 months ago. We had about eight, nine months steady work between a couple of jobs like that, you know. Although he's not doing anything now, you know. That's the reason why I have this little outfit now, you know.
